descriptionChirho: A proper noun designating one of the five major Philistine cities, located on the Mediterranean coast of Canaan (modern Ashkelon, Israel). Referenced in contexts of Israelite conquest (Judg 1:18, capturing Ashkelon and its territory), Samson's exploits (Judg 14:19, striking down thirty men of Ashkelon), the plague of tumors sent upon the Philistines (1 Sam 6:17, a golden tumor for Ashkelon), prophetic oracles of judgment against Philistia (Jer 25:20; 47:5, 7; Amos 1:8; Zeph 2:4, 7; Zech 9:5), and David's lament over Saul (2 Sam 1:20, 'tell it not in Gath, proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon'). Spelling variants (Ashqelon / Ashkelon) and prepositional forms (from Ashkelon, for Ashkelon, and Ashkelon) are orthographic and syntactic variations referring to the same city, not distinct lexical senses.
